design_note: The previous labs inspect deletion and audit receipts. This example adds derivation provenance before reuse: a shorter summary remains linked to the confidential record from which it was made. The local purpose rule remains explicit instead of implying that provenance metadata itself grants or denies access.

source.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
source.concept: Derivation records connect an entity to the source entity from which it was transformed or constructed. Optional activity and usage information can make that lineage more precise.
source.scope: The customer record, summary and support-only policy are fictional. PROV describes provenance; it does not prescribe classification inheritance or grant processing permission.

lesson.title: A shorter summary keeps a longer lineage
lesson.intro: ShopAssist summarizes confidential case C-7 into S-7. The summary still identifies the customer. A separate marketing job requests S-7, but the reviewed handling rule permits support use only.

relations: S-7 retains the C-7 derivation reference.
Every reuse checks its own purpose and principal.

read: The summary is a separate artifact with a link to its source.
It still contains a customer identifier and retains the handling class.
The marketing purpose fails the stated reuse rule even if storage is approved.
lesson.question: Does shortening C-7 into S-7 make the marketing request permissible?
lesson.answer: No. The summary remains identifiable confidential content, and the explicit rule restricts it to support. The derivation link helps locate the applicable source policy; it does not supply authority. A changed use or classification requires its own reviewed basis.
lesson.takeaway: Preserve lineage and recheck purpose when reusing derived content.
lesson.assumption: Fictional handling policy and identified summary; no anonymization or legal compliance claim. Containers show records and authority, not execution order.
